body: Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 2: A person qualifies for an entitlement under the family scheme if, for an entitlement period, they meet the qualifying criteria in sections MC 3 to MC 7 and the continuing requirements in section MC 8.
Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 3: The first family scheme requirement is that the person referred to in section MC 2 is 16 or older.
Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 4: The second family scheme requirement is that the person referred to in section MC 2 is the principal caregiver for 1 or more dependent children.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 5: The third family scheme requirement is that the person or child meets residence requirements, or the person is entitled to an emergency benefit under Social Security Act 2018 section 63 or 64. A person meets the residence requirements if they have been both a New Zealand resident and present in New Zealand for a continuous period of 12 months at any time, are resident in New Zealand under section YD 1 on credit days, and are not a transitional resident or the spouse or partner of a transitional resident. A child meets the residence requirements if the child is both a New Zealand resident and present in New Zealand for the entitlement period.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 6: Despite sections MC 3 to MC 5, a person does not qualify for an abating WFF tax credit or Best Start tax credit if, during the relationship period, they receive a Veterans' Support Act parent's allowance or children's pension. A person does not qualify for an in-work tax credit, parental tax credit, or minimum family tax credit if, during the relationship period, they receive a main benefit, parent's allowance, or children's pension. A person does not qualify for a Best Start tax credit for a dependent child and period if they receive a parental leave payment, preterm baby payment, parental tax credit, parent's allowance, or children's pension for that child or period.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 7: If spouses or partners each meet the qualifying criteria for different dependent children during an entitlement period, one person is treated as meeting the qualifying criteria for all those children and the other is treated as not meeting them. For WFF tax credits other than the in-work tax credit, the Commissioner determines which person meets the criteria.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 8: A person meeting the qualifying criteria must also meet continuing requirements throughout the entitlement period: the person meets the qualifying criteria on each day; a spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner does not start or stop on any day; the person does not start or stop being principal caregiver of a dependent child except on the first or last day; a child for whom the person is principal caregiver does not stop being a dependent child except on the first or last day; WFF tax credit composition does not change except on the first or last day; and protected family tax credit status does not start or stop except on the first or last day. Section MD 6(2) overrides this section for the in-work tax credit.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 9: A person is entitled to a tax credit under sections MD 1 and ME 1 for a person aged 18 who is not financially independent and is attending school or a tertiary educational establishment. The Commissioner determines the period, which ends on or before the first day fixed for payments of tax-credit instalments in the calendar year following the year in which the person turns 18.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 10: A principal caregiver is the person the Commissioner considers has primary responsibility for day-to-day care of a dependent child other than temporarily, excluding a body of persons, certain spouses or partners of non-electing transitional residents, and proprietors or employees of specified residences or institutions. For family tax credit, Best Start, and child tax credit purposes, a person is principal caregiver if they live apart from another person who qualifies under MC 2 for the child and have exclusive care for periods totaling at least one-third of a 4-month period, the tax year, or the parental-tax-credit entitlement period. For the in-work tax credit, the exclusive-care periods must total at least one-third of a 4-month period or the tax year. For parental tax credit, exclusive care must total at least one-third of the parental entitlement period.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MC 11: In subparts MB to MG and MZ, a relationship period is an unbroken period in a tax year, and an entitlement period for a person is a period forming all or part of a relationship period during which the person meets the section MC 8 continuing requirements. If a day is part of more than 1 entitlement period or relationship period, the day is treated as part only of the period that the Commissioner determines is fair.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 4: A person is entitled to an in-work tax credit for a child if, for an entitlement period, the person meets the 5 requirements of sections MD 5 to MD 9. If 2 persons are entitled to an in-work tax credit or child tax credit for a child for an entitlement period, each entitlement is not affected by the other.
Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 5: The first requirement for entitlement to an in-work tax credit is that the person referred to in section MD 4 is 16 or older.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 6: The second requirement for entitlement to an in-work tax credit is that the person referred to in section MD 4 is principal caregiver for a child who is financially dependent on them. A child for whom Oranga Tamariki Act section 363 payments are made, or for whom an orphan's benefit or unsupported child's benefit is paid, is treated as financially dependent on the person. This override applies despite section MC 8.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 7: The third requirement for entitlement to an in-work tax credit is that the person or child referred to in section MD 4 meets residence requirements. A person meets the requirements if they have been both a New Zealand resident and present in New Zealand for a continuous period of 12 months at any time, are resident in New Zealand under section YD 1 on days for which an MD 1 tax credit arises, and are neither a transitional resident nor the spouse or partner of one. A child meets the requirements if resident and present in New Zealand for the entitlement period.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 8: The fourth requirement for entitlement to an in-work tax credit is that the person referred to in section MD 4 and their spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner do not receive a main benefit, a basic grant and independent circumstances grant under regulations made under Education and Training Act 2020 section 645 or substituted enactment, or a Veterans' Support Act parent's allowance or children's pension.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 9: The fifth requirement for entitlement to an in-work tax credit is that the person or their spouse or partner is normally an earner and either derives qualifying income, derives specified compensation, meets the alternative 14 day concession, or, for a close company earner, is a major shareholder and the company derives gross income. Qualifying income includes allowed PAYE income payments, non-PAYE income to which sections RD 3B or RD 3C apply, income from a business carried on for profit, and specified personal service rehabilitation payment income, excluding specified PAYE payments and pre-2006 incapacity payments. A person meets the requirement through legacy compensation if they received a child tax credit for a period ending 31 March 2006, suffered incapacity between 1 January 2006 and 31 March 2006 inclusive, weekly compensation is being or will be paid, and the legacy full-time-earner and formula conditions are met. A person also meets the requirement if normally deriving qualifying income as a full-time earner but, in a 1-week period, works less or not at all because of a child's birth and is entitled to parental tax credit for the child. A person also meets the requirement if they do not derive income or otherwise do not meet the fifth requirement but met it within the last 14 days.
